summary: Diagnose nose scan quality, glasses-nose seating, and jitter at angles in ar/

capture.mechanism: Raw MediaPipe landmarks (numFaces:2, unsmoothed) + raw pose matrix enter frame.js: the raw pose is composed onto scene.head (frame.js:222-229, rawHeadWorld kept so all measurement inverts the pose the landmarks were solved with). measureAnchors (anchors.js:323) ray-carries ~12 landmarks into face space at borrowed-canonical camera depth blended with a one-frame-stale depth fit (frame.js:243, anchors.js:338-377), clamped (anchors.js:485). A latched pose gate (frame.js:267-273; yaw 0.25 [~9 deg true], pitch 0.26, roll 0.30, exit at 1.15x) decides 'measuring'; only measuring frames feed the 31-sample median window (frame.js:284-289, anchors.js:554) whose scalars pass commitFit deadbands (frame.js:507-538). Anchors are then assembled with bridge POSITION live every frame and proportions carried (frame.js:355-373). updateOccluder (occluder.js:653) then runs the 'scan': fitLandmarkDepth (occluder.js:574-645) fits one global affine a*z_mp+b of MediaPipe's relative z onto camera depth — slope from camera geometry (-2*dist*tan(fov/2)*aspect, occluder.js:625-633), offset from the pose, gated/blended by a smoothstep of r2 over [0.88,0.92] (occluder.js:303-304,642-644). carryLandmarks (anchors.js:251-315) walks each of 468 view rays to the blended depth (clamp +/-1.6 cm, occluder.js:277). measureShape (occluder.js:736-826) turns observed-minus-canonical into per-vertex offsets, weighted by a facing ramp (FACING_HOLD -0.45 to FACING_TRUST -0.05, occluder.js:195-196) times a 96^2 self-occlusion depth grid hold (VIS_BIAS 0.35 + VIS_GRAZE 1.0, VIS_RAMP 0.5, occluder.js:223-247,843-929), eased by an EMA with SHAPE_TAU=0.10 s (occluder.js:171,758; first sample adopted whole per vertex times facing), offsets clamped +/-2 cm. When accumulated drift exceeds 0.2 mm (SURFACE_DEADBAND, occluder.js:307) the surface rebuilds: Richardson-compensated control mesh (subdivide.js:283-298) -> Loop x2 subdivision (7.3 mm nose edges -> 1.8 mm, occluder.js:92, subdivide.js) -> skull reloft (head.js:165) -> 1-mm-cell depth field over a 9x12 cm nose window (nose.js:46-131) -> relief inward by PAD_SINK+feather+0.01 = 1.8 mm capped at 4 px (occluder.js:132,156). The occluder is translated so its bridge lands exactly on anchors.bridge, raw, every frame (occluder.js:717-731). solvePlacement sets height optically along bridgeUp (fit.js:480-492) and seat() (nose.js:226-278) finds one scalar push along +Z — worst interference over the model's bridge contacts against that same field, minus PAD_SINK 0.5 mm, clamped 1.2 cm — eased at SEAT_TAU=0.15 s (frame.js:64,437-448). Seat surface, occluder depth buffer, and soft mask are the same triangles by construction (occluder.js:940-973, fit.js:510-521).

causes.title: Nose depth is never measured — it is a 1-DOF offset on a learned prior
causes.mechanism: The only person-specific depth information anywhere in the scan is MediaPipe's relative z field, which is itself a neural model's plausible-face guess (it regresses individuals toward the average face internally, the same regression-to-mean the camera-slope fix removed only at the global-gain level). fitLandmarkDepth solves ONE offset b for the whole face (slope fixed by camera geometry), so the fitted surface is 'MediaPipe's z field, rigidly placed'. There is no mechanism that observes THIS nose's tip protrusion, ridge height, or sidewall slope independently of that prior. Below r2=0.88 the weight is zero and the entire nose depth silently becomes the canonical average nose; between 0.88 and 0.92 it is a blend of the two.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:574-645 (single global affine; slope at 625-633, weight at 642-644), anchors.js:288-299 (blend + clamp), occluder.js:303-304 (band). Only calibration point ever taken: one capture at 10.6 deg yaw (prior 2026-08-15 review, confirmed). depthClamped counter exists as instrument (occluder.js:277,753).
causes.magnitude: Individual nose protrusion differs from canonical by +/-5-10 mm; sidewall slope is 8 mm per cm of x travel (nose.js:47), so mm-scale depth error is mm-scale seat error. The pre-fix regression measured 18.5% flattening while reporting r2=0.971 — proof r2 cannot see gain/shape error in the z field itself. At r2<0.88, 100% of nose depth is the average head's.
causes.fixDirection: Replace 'trust the z prior' with measurement: accumulate silhouette/parallax constraints across poses (see opportunities) into a persistent per-vertex depth correction with per-vertex confidence; keep the camera-slope affine as the frame-one prior only.

causes.title: The r2 gate is whole-face and yaw-inflated — nose quality is invisible to it
causes.mechanism: r2 is computed over all 468 landmarks. At yaw, the rigid rotation ramp dominates depth variance, so r2 INFLATES exactly when the far-side landmarks are hallucinated (prior finding, adversarially confirmed): the gate reports healthy on garbage, and the hallucinated far sidewall enters the fit that sets the offset for the whole nose. Conversely a frame whose nose z is bad but whose cheeks are fine passes. No per-region residual is ever computed, though the running sums to do it are already in the loop.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:579-603 (sums over all landmarks, r2 at 603); prior finding ar-occlusion-review-findings (r2 inflates with yaw); measureVisibility gates the DEFORM against hallucination (occluder.js:771) but nothing gates the FIT's input landmarks.
causes.magnitude: Unbounded in principle at yaw (fit offset polluted by hallucinated far side, clamped only at +/-1.6 cm); in the 0.88-0.92 band the whole nose morphs between fitted and average protrusion — several mm of shape change riding on a scalar.
causes.fixDirection: Weight the fit's input by the same visibility grid the deform already trusts; compute nose-window residual separately; de-mean per region.

causes.title: 20 landmarks on the pad strip, and subdivision adds smoothness, not information
causes.mechanism: Counted on the canonical mesh: 98 of 468 vertices lie in a generous nose box, but only 20 (10 per side) lie in the strip where pads bear (|x| 0.5-1.7 cm, bridge.y-1.5 to +0.3), spaced 4-6 mm. Loop x2 subdivision (applied once in createOccluder, occluder.js:325, with the compensation solve so the limit surface interpolates the 468) makes the surface between landmarks smooth, but every subdivided vertex is a weighted average of the same 20 measurements — a nose bump, asymmetry, or a narrow high bridge between landmarks is unrepresentable regardless of tessellation.
causes.evidence: Measured from ar/assets/face/canonical_face_model.obj (this session): pad-strip verts 114,122,128,174,188,196,233,243,244,245 + mirrors, spacing 4-6 mm. Subdivision applied occluder.js:325; compensation subdivide.js:283-298. LM sidewall pairs at canonical-face.js:35-38.
causes.magnitude: Surface features under ~5 mm wavelength on the sidewall cannot be captured at all; the 4-6 mm sampling is the resolution floor of any redesign that keeps landmark-only input.
causes.fixDirection: Any real nose capture needs a signal denser than landmarks on this strip (silhouette curve at yaw, or photometric/depth-from-parallax) — not more subdivision.

causes.title: The shape never converges — a 0.1 s EMA with no memory, no confidence, chasing forever
causes.mechanism: offsets is a single Float32Array updated per frame at rate alpha*facing with alpha=1-exp(-dt/0.10) (~0.28 at 30 fps). A vertex seen for ten minutes is treated identically to one seen for three frames; white landmark noise passes into the surface at ~0.4x amplitude (EMA variance factor sqrt(a/(2-a))); the shape is by design view-dependent and is effectively 'the last ~300 ms of frames'. Convergence is not representable in the data model: there is no per-vertex sample count, variance, or pose-coverage record — only hasShape (a boolean) and the current EMA state. Resets: deform toggle (occluder.js:697-707) and occluder creation; remeasure() (frame.js:573) resets anchors/seat but NOT the shape.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:171 (SHAPE_TAU), 758 (alpha), 810-817 (EMA), 424 (data model: offsets only), 443 (hasShape); frame.js:573-580 (remeasure does not touch occluder).
causes.magnitude: Time constant 0.10 s; noise attenuation only ~2.5x in amplitude; a 1 mm landmark jitter is a ~0.4 mm surface shimmer feeding the 0.2 mm rebuild deadband. The scan can never be better than slightly-smoothed single-frame quality.
causes.fixDirection: Split the state: a fast view-locked correction (keeps the invariant that the mesh covers THIS image) layered on a slowly-converging person model with per-vertex confidence that only improves. Median/robust accumulation per vertex is the surface analogue of the 31-sample anchor window that already works for scalars.

causes.title: Facing normals are canonical, and yaw frames are held rather than learned from
causes.mechanism: The facing test dots the camera direction against baseNormals computed once from the CANONICAL mesh (occluder.js:415-419, 797) — a person-specific sidewall that slopes differently never updates its own trust geometry. More fundamentally, HOLD is the only response to a difficult pose: at yaw the near nose ridge is a true silhouette (the best-observed curve in the image, constraining protrusion absolutely via parallax against the cheek) and the pipeline's response is to freeze the far side and keep EMA-ing the near side in x/y only.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:195-196 (ramp), 415-419 (canonical normals), 843-929 (visibility grid computes exactly the cover geometry a silhouette extractor would need, then discards it each frame).
causes.magnitude: Qualitative but structural: the one observation geometry that measures nose depth without the z prior is systematically discarded; the diag/f00-f09 complaint captures (roll+pitch) are precisely such poses and are consumed by nothing (verified: only face-a.jpg/face-b.jpg referenced, main.js:54-55, pipeline-check.js:49).

causes.title: The seat is one scalar: push along +Z — no height coupling, no roll, no two-pad contact
causes.mechanism: seat() computes the worst interference over the model's bridge contacts and pushes the whole frame out along face +Z (nose.js:226-278); height was already fixed by the pupil-height optics along bridgeUp (fit.js:480-492) and orientation comes rigidly from the pose. Real glasses settle DOWN the nose wedge until the pads stop them — height, standoff, and pad contact are one coupled solve. Here they are decoupled: on a narrow/low bridge the frame is held at optical height and pushed far off the face (floats); on a wide nose it is pushed out barely and reads as buried; on an asymmetric nose the worst-interference rule rests the frame on ONE pad and nothing rolls it into two-point contact. This is the structural reason the interaction 'is not good at all' — it cannot be fixed by a better surface alone.
causes.evidence: nose.js:226-278 (single push, worst-over-contacts at 251-269, PAD_SINK subtraction at 274), fit.js:510-521 (seat applied after height), fit.js:480-492 (height solve independent).
causes.magnitude: The nose falls away 5.5 mm at 7 mm off centreline (nose.js:9-17), so the height-standoff coupling the solve ignores is worth ~0.8 mm of standoff per mm of vertical placement error; catalogue measurements in the module header show 4.2 mm hover to 1.7 mm burial across four frames from exactly this class of decoupling. Push clamp 1.2 cm; PAD_SINK fixed 0.5 mm for all frames and skin.
causes.fixDirection: Solve height + standoff (+ optionally pitch) jointly against the wedge: slide along bridgeUp until pad contacts balance, with the pupil-height target as a soft cost, not a fixed constraint.

causes.title: The seat solves against the fitted nose, so every scan error is a seat error 1:1
causes.mechanism: The single-surface guarantee (correct, keep it) means the seat inherits the scan's depth error exactly: the field is rasterised from the deformed skin whose nose depth is scan-cause-1's affine guess or the canonical fallback. A sidewall drawn 2 mm too far forward seats the frame 2 mm too far out and the occluder hides the discrepancy by construction — the system is self-consistent and wrong together, which is why it reads as 'the interaction with the nose' rather than as a visible hole.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:940-973 (field from skin), nose.js:91-101 (rebuild), fit.js:511 (surfaceOf preferred), occluder.js:1013-1015.
causes.magnitude: mm-scale, tracking scan error; the sidewall's 8 mm/cm slope converts any lateral landmark bias into depth error at ~0.8x.

causes.title: The bridge pin's depth still falls back to canonical exactly at the point everything hangs from
causes.mechanism: anchors.bridge is measured live every frame; its depth is borrowed-canonical blended with the (one-frame-stale) fit by fitWeight, and at r2<=0.88 the blend weight is zero — the pin depth is the AVERAGE head's at the one point the frame and the occluder are both translated to. Head-on that error is pure z and the seat absorbs it; at tilt/yaw it rotates into the image and pushes frame + occluder together sideways/forward off the nose, invisible to every internal consistency check.
causes.evidence: anchors.js:353-377 (blend, guess=borrowed at weight 0), frame.js:243 (stale fit), occluder.js:717-731 (occluder translated onto same pin); prior finding confirmed 2026-08-15.
causes.magnitude: Individual bridge-depth error up to ~1 cm; projects into the image as sin(pose angle) — ~3.4 mm sideways at 20 deg, ~10+ screen px on the close-up captures.

causes.title: The depth-fit weight band turns r2 noise into whole-nose depth flicker
causes.mechanism: weight is a smoothstep of r2 over a band only 0.04 wide (0.88-0.92), max derivative 37.5 per unit r2. Frame-to-frame r2 noise of just +/-0.005 moves the weight by up to ~0.19, and every fitted depth — all 468 vertices AND the bridge anchor — moves by weight-delta times (solved-borrowed), which the clamp allows up to 16 mm. The band is exactly where difficult poses live (r2 degrades toward it at yaw, while also being yaw-inflated), so the nose visibly breathes in depth at the very angles the user complains about; the seat re-solves against the moving field each rebuild.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:303-304,642-644 (band + smoothstep), anchors.js:262,339 (same weight applied to recovery and bridge), occluder.js:296-302 (comment admits the band was added to fix the binary flip — the residual analogue remains).
causes.magnitude: Up to ~0.19 x |solved-borrowed| per frame near the band: with a typical 5 mm fitted-vs-borrowed nose difference, ~1 mm/frame depth flicker; worst case (clamp-railed) ~3 mm/frame. SHAPE_TAU smooths the surface's copy to ~0.4x but the bridge anchor's copy is UNSMOOTHED and moves the whole assembly.
causes.fixDirection: Ease the weight itself in time (it is a slow global quantity), or gate on a robust multi-frame r2 median; never let an unsmoothed scalar multiply a centimetre-scale disagreement.

causes.title: The bridge pin rides raw landmarks with zero filtering, and the landmark itself degrades at angle
causes.mechanism: By deliberate invariant, position is re-measured every frame and applied raw (frame.js:355-357 'bridge stays live at EVERY pose'; occluder.js:717-731 'no deadband'). The entire jitter budget of frame + occluder position is therefore whatever MediaPipe's bridge landmark does frame to frame — and at yaw/roll the bridge landmark slides across the nose as one side occludes (documented at frame.js:22-25). Nothing distinguishes 'noise' from 'motion' on this signal; the pose smoother smooths the head pose but the pin bypasses it entirely.
causes.evidence: frame.js:231-244 (raw measurement), 355-357; occluder.js:717-724; frame.js:22-25 (bridge slide at yaw acknowledged).
causes.magnitude: ~0.3-0.5 mm frontal (sub-pixel landmark noise at typical scale) — invisible; multi-mm at high yaw/roll where the landmark slides — this is the 'especially in difficult angles' signature. Amplified by the depth flicker above at tilt (depth error rotates into image).
causes.fixDirection: The invariant says position is re-measured every frame — it does not forbid a motion-aware filter ON the measurement (e.g., OneEuro at lead 0 on the bridge in face space), which preserves frame-lock while removing the noise floor.

causes.title: Gate-crossing steps: the latched measuring flag hard-swaps observed vs carried fields
causes.mechanism: When the latch flips (enter at yaw~9deg/pitch15deg/roll17deg true, exit at 1.15x), eyeLineY, bridgeUp, and both ear rest points step between live-observed and carried-median values in a single frame (frame.js:355-372). The latch stops oscillation, but each crossing is still a discrete step in vertical placement and arm aim — and a user exploring 'difficult angles' crosses it constantly.
causes.evidence: frame.js:267-273 (latch), 355-372 (swaps); the latch comment itself documents the twitch it half-fixed.
causes.magnitude: mm-scale one-frame steps (observed-vs-carried differ by accumulated drift + noise); vertical steps move the frame along bridgeUp which has a forward component, so they read as a small pop.

causes.title: Shape churn cascades into seat breathing through the rebuild deadband
causes.mechanism: Landmark noise passes the EMA at ~0.4x amplitude into skin; accumulated drift crosses SURFACE_DEADBAND=0.2 mm every few frames, triggering rebuild -> new depth field -> seat() finds a slightly different worst-contact -> push changes -> eased at SEAT_TAU 0.15 s. The frame is thus never at rest: it breathes at the beat frequency of rebuilds, and at difficult angles the facing/visibility weights add bands of vertices toggling between update and hold (smoothstep ramps, but the vertex SET crossing them changes discretely), making the far boundary and the field under the far pad crawl.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:307 (deadband), 819-825 (drift), frame.js:64,437-448 (seat easing); occluder.js:798-807 (per-frame weight recompute).
causes.magnitude: Sub-mm per event but continuous; visible as low-amplitude 'does not stand still completely' rather than as pops. rebuilds counter (occluder.js:459) can quantify the rate live.

keep: The frame-locked measurement discipline: raw pose held in rawHeadWorld (frame.js:222-229) and every measurement inverting the pose its landmarks were solved with — this is correct and rare; any redesign must keep it.
carryLandmarks (anchors.js:251-315): the ray-through-landmark recovery is the right x/y measurement machinery at any pose; a redesign changes what depth it walks to, not the mechanism.

The single-surface guarantee: seat field, occluder depth buffer, and soft mask rasterised from one vertex array (occluder.js:940-973, nose.js:91-101, fit.js:510-521, surfaceOf) — disagreement is impossible by construction. Rebuild the shape estimator INSIDE this contract.

The subdivision plan (subdivide.js): precomputed CSR Loop with the Richardson compensation solve so the limit surface interpolates measurements — cheap (warm 3 passes), correct, and exactly what a denser future measurement set would also need.

measureVisibility (occluder.js:843-929): the 96^2 direction-space depth grid is the right observability primitive; reuse it as the per-vertex confidence input for any accumulating estimator, and as the silhouette extractor for parallax constraints.

fitLandmarkDepth's camera-derived slope (occluder.js:625-633): slope from -2*d*tan(fov/2)*aspect instead of regression killed an 18.5% flattening; the principle (never let a regression borrow the average face's gain) survives any redesign as the frame-one prior.
The iris metric scale + PD gate (anchors.js:182-232, canonical-face.js:82-92): the only absolute ruler, correctly measured at the iris plane only.

The 31-sample median anchor window + commitFit deadbands + identity tolerance (anchors.js:554-595, frame.js:93-135, 507-557): the scalar convergence model is right — it is the surface that lacks an equivalent.
The head shell loft, profile table, and pinna dishes (head.js): solves temple occlusion independently of the nose problem; nothing about the redesign touches it.
The relief derivation chain PAD_SINK -> OCCLUDER_RELIEF -> MAX_RELIEF_PX cap (occluder.js:115-156) and the soft occlusion mask: physically derived, screen-aware, and the reason holes stopped.
Diagnostics already wired: depthClamped, rebuilds counters, window.__ar reporting (occluder.js:277,459) — the redesign's harness should assert on them.
opportunities: Yaw parallax is discarded: at 15-40 deg the near nose ridge is a true silhouette against the cheek — an absolute protrusion measurement needing no z prior. measureVisibility already computes per-vertex cover depth (the exact geometry of the silhouette) and throws it away every frame; two poses ~20 deg apart triangulate nose depth outright. The pipeline currently responds to these frames with HOLD.

diag/f00-f09 (ar/assets/samples/diag/) — the user's own complaint captures, roll+pitch on a pillow — are consumed by nothing (verified: only face-a/face-b referenced in main.js:54-55 and pipeline-check.js:49). They are a ready-made regression set for all three symptoms.

No surface analogue of the anchor median window: per-vertex confidence/persistence is representable today as one extra Float32Array + count; the facing*visibility weight already computed per frame (occluder.js:798-807) is the correct accumulation weight and is currently used once and dropped.

Per-region fit residuals are free: the running sums in fitLandmarkDepth (occluder.js:579-591) restricted to the nose window give a nose-specific r2/residual that the global gate cannot see; same loop, no extra cost.

MediaPipe's z field could be temporally median-filtered per vertex in face space BEFORE the affine fit — the fit is currently instantaneous per frame, so z noise enters twice (through the fit's b and through each landmark's own z).

The iris ruler could calibrate the assumed 63-deg FOV: metricScale as a function of pose distance over a session over-determines the true focal length, which currently biases the depth-fit slope by up to ~25% and every absolute standoff with it.
depthClamped and r2 are reported but feed nothing back: a frame with railed depth clamps is a bad-fit frame and could down-weight itself.

numFaces:2 delivers raw landmarks on purpose — the raw noise floor per landmark is measurable online (variance over a still second) and would let trust weights be per-landmark empirical instead of geometric guesses (FACING/VIS constants).

The seat solve has all inputs needed for a coupled height+standoff wedge solve already in face space (bridgeUp, contacts, the depth field); no new measurement is required to fix seat-cause-1 — it is a solver change.

seat.mechanism: LOAD TIME (once per asset): analyseModel (ar/src/fit.js:44) finds two things on the frame: a single hang point — findNoseContact (fit.js:128-178), centreline column widened until >=30 verts, rearmost 20% z-band averaged, x pinned to centreline — and a contact SET — findBridgeSurface (fit.js:202-236), the whole central column (+-13% of frame width), binned at ~0.8mm cells in x/y, keeping the rearmost vertex per bin (a few hundred points). PER FRAME: updateFrame (ar/src/frame.js:176) measures anchors under the raw pose, then updateOccluder deforms the 468-vertex face by per-vertex facing/self-occlusion-weighted easing (SHAPE_TAU 0.10s, occluder.js:171, 736-826) with landmark-z protrusion blended by the r2 smoothstep 0.88-0.92 (occluder.js:303-304, 642-644); whenever accumulated vertex drift >= 0.2mm (SURFACE_DEADBAND, occluder.js:307) rebuildSurface (occluder.js:940-973) re-rasterises the subdivided skin (~17.7k window triangles) into the seat field — a 91x121 grid of 1mm cells over x[-4.5,4.5], y[-5,7] cm keeping max-z per cell (nose.js:46-48, 65-131). solvePlacement (fit.js:385-528) then runs in strict order: scale (physical: FACE_UNITS_PER_METRE, fit.js:410) -> orientation (constant pantoscopicTilt 8 deg minus the asset's measured rake, about X only, fit.js:430-434) -> position (hang noseContact on anchors.bridge x/y/z, fit.js:442-451) -> vertical (pupil-height slide along bridgeUp until pupils sit at 0.45 of lens height, clamped +-1.5cm, fit.js:464-492) -> seat: seat() (nose.js:226-278) transforms every contact by the placed matrix, queries the field bilinearly in bridge-relative coordinates (nose.js:251-257; bridge x/y/z errors cancel exactly by construction), computes interference = (skin+shiftZ) - placed.z per contact, takes the WORST (max), subtracts PAD_SINK 0.5mm (nose.js:207), clamps to +-1.5cm (maxNoseSeat, fit.js:352), and returns ONE scalar: a z push. fit.js:521 applies it; frame.js:437-448 eases it through SEAT_TAU 0.15s (frame.js:64) — the only smoothed quantity in the placement. The drawn occluder is the same skin relieved inward 1.8mm along normals (OCCLUDER_RELIEF = PAD_SINK + feather + margin, occluder.js:132, 511-534) so the seated worst contact stays visible. Output of the entire contact model: a single eased z translation. No lateral, no vertical, no roll, no tilt comes from contact.

causes.title: Resting height is an optical target, not a contact equilibrium — the solve structurally cannot express sliding down the nose wedge
causes.mechanism: Real glasses slide down the nasal wedge under gravity until pad separation equals nose width at that height; resting height (and with it lens height and standoff) is a FUNCTION of nose geometry and the frame's DBL. In this pipeline height is decided BEFORE any contact is consulted: the pupil slide (fit.js:464-492) places the frame so pupils sit at pupilTarget 0.45 of the lens, clamped +-1.5cm, and the seat then only pushes along z. So every frame sits at the optically ideal height on every face — a wide-bridge frame on a narrow nose that should slide visibly low sits exactly where a narrow-bridge frame does. The frame never LOOKS like it is resting on the nose because its height carries no information about the nose. This is the structural core of 'the interaction is not good at all': the one thing a viewer's eye checks — does the frame hang where this nose would carry it — is the one thing the solve cannot produce.
causes.evidence: fit.js:464-492 (height from eyeLineY/pupilTarget, no nose term); fit.js:495-522 (seat is z-only, runs after height is settled and 'cannot undo any of their work' by design); nose width is measured every frame (anchors.js:398-449) and consumed by nothing in the seat since the warp removal (nose.js:230-245)

Two frames 4mm apart in DBL should rest ~7-8mm apart in height; today they render at identical height. Across faces, a nose 15% narrower (3.5mm) should drop the same frame ~6-7mm; today: 0.
causes.fixDirection: Invert the causality: solve height and standoff TOGETHER as a descent along bridgeUp — lower the frame until the left and right pad-region contact sets both bear on the field (width-at-height is derivable from the existing field by finding where depthAt crosses the pad depth). Keep pupilHeightInLens (fit.js:539-551) but demote it from constraint to reported verdict — it is the optician's honest fit measure, and 'this frame sits low on you' is a feature of a try-on, not a bug.

causes.title: The contact model is single-point tangency: one scalar z push at the worst contact — no second bearing, no roll, no emergent tilt
causes.mechanism: seat() reduces several hundred contact samples to max(interference) - PAD_SINK (nose.js:249-277). Whichever single bin touches first carries the whole frame; every other contact — including the entire opposite pad — is left wherever that one push puts it. Real glasses bear on TWO nasal sidewalls simultaneously; the two-sided bearing is what makes contact read as load-bearing. With one DOF the frame reads as pinned in space and pressed against the nose at one point: on any asymmetric observation (and at yaw the field is always asymmetric — near side re-pinned, far side carried) one pad touches and the other floats by the full asymmetry. Roll is absent everywhere (prior review finding: no roll handling in the pipeline), and pantoscopic tilt is a constant 8 deg for every face (fit.js:330, 430-434) rather than emerging from pad contact plus temple line, so the frame's attitude never responds to the nose either.
causes.evidence: nose.js:249-277 (single worst-point max, push is the only output); fit.js:430-434 (tilt constant, about X only); the left/right identity of contacts is discarded — nothing splits the sample set by side
causes.magnitude: Second-side float equals observed nose asymmetry plus field asymmetry at yaw: ~1-3mm typical, worse in the user's roll+pitch diag poses. The visible read is binary though: single-point tangency plus uniform 0.5mm PAD_SINK makes contact look painted-on rather than bearing, at every angle.
causes.fixDirection: Solve 2-3 DOF static equilibrium instead of 1: split noseContacts by side of centreline (the set already carries both, harness asserts spread across the centreline at pipeline-check.js:507-526), require both sides to bear, let roll and height balance them. Tilt could then take a face-dependent component from the contact normal.

causes.title: The seat — a face constant — is re-derived every frame from a field that morphs with trust, and the max() argmax flips discretely
causes.mechanism: The resting standoff of rigid glasses on a rigid face is a constant, but the pipeline recomputes it per frame against a surface that is itself moving: rebuildSurface fires on 0.2mm of accumulated vertex drift (occluder.js:307) — i.e. essentially continuously during head motion — from a skin whose vertices are individually eased (SHAPE_TAU 0.1s) under facing-trust ramps (occluder.js:195-196), self-occlusion holds (occluder.js:223-247), and the landmark-depth blend whose weight rides r2 through the 0.88-0.92 band (occluder.js:303-304). At 'difficult angles' — exactly where the user complains — the far sidewall is held at carried shape while the near side re-pins, r2 inflates with yaw (prior confirmed finding: it can report healthy on garbage), and the nose's protrusion breathes between fitted and borrowed depth. The push follows every one of these morphs. On top of that, max() over ~hundreds of contacts is non-smooth: when the resting contact flips between bins (saddle vs pad, near vs far), the push steps by the depth gap between the candidates. SEAT_TAU 0.15s (frame.js:64, 437-448) is the only defense — it smears steps over ~0.45s instead of removing them, which reads as the frame slowly breathing in and out of the face while the head holds a hard pose. Note what does NOT drive seat jitter: bridge x/y/z noise cancels exactly in seat()'s bridge-relative formulation (nose.js:247-257 + fit.js:442-446), and eyeLineY is frozen outside the measuring latch (frame.js:355-360) — so at difficult angles the field morph is close to the WHOLE driver, which matches the complaint being worst there.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:307 (SURFACE_DEADBAND 0.02cm), occluder.js:171 (SHAPE_TAU), occluder.js:303-304 + 642-644 (r2 blend), nose.js:262-269 (worst-contact argmax), frame.js:64+437-448 (SEAT_TAU easing, the only filter); prior 2026-08-15 review: r2 inflates with yaw, calibrated at one 10.6-deg capture
causes.magnitude: A depth-fit weight excursion morphs nose protrusion by up to the real fitted-vs-canonical gap, ~2-5mm (clamped at DEPTH_LIMIT 16mm), paced by SHAPE_TAU ~0.3s; contact-flip steps ~0.5-2mm; both pass through SEAT_TAU as visible mm-scale z breathing over ~0.5s. At 45cm, 1mm of z is ~1.5-2px — a 3mm breathe is a plainly visible 5-6px pulse of standoff.
causes.fixDirection: Separate the timescales: the resting configuration (height-on-wedge, standoff, roll) is a face constant — solve it against the converged/deadbanded shape estimate slowly (deadband + long tau, or solve only on shape-rebuild events), and let per-frame work be pure re-pinning of position/orientation. Replace max() with a soft-max or two-sided bearing solve so the argmax cannot flip discretely.

causes.title: The field answers the wrong query for seating: depth-under-(x,y) can express 'through the skin' but not 'bearing on a sidewall'
causes.mechanism: buildFaceSurface keeps max-z per 1mm cell — a viewpoint height field along face z (nose.js:65-131). That is exactly right for the question it was built for (is this frame vertex behind the drawn surface) and structurally unable to express the question real seating asks (at what height does the wedge's width equal the pad separation; what is the sidewall's surface normal where the pad bears). The z-only push inherits this: clearance is created along the axis the field is parameterised in, so a pad approaching a steep sidewall laterally is 'resolved' by pulling the whole frame forward instead of letting it ride up the wedge — which is why every fit error, whatever its true direction, becomes a standoff error. The wedge information IS in the array (the sidewall fall-off is resolved at 1mm cells, nose.js:47), it is just never queried in wedge terms.
causes.evidence: nose.js:65-131 (max-z rasterisation, depthAt(x,y) is the only query); nose.js:216-224 (push deliberately along +Z only); nose.js:9-11 and pipeline-check.js:420-424 (the fall-off — 5.5mm at 7mm off centreline — is documented and asserted, then used only as motivation for the z push)
causes.magnitude: Qualitative but structural: with one query primitive the solve has one DOF available no matter how good the data is. The 5.5mm/7mm sidewall slope means the same field, queried as width-at-height, resolves the wedge to ~1mm — the data for a real seat is already paid for.
causes.fixDirection: Add wedge queries on the existing field (widthAt(y, padDepth), normalAt(x,y) from finite differences) rather than a new data structure. The field machinery itself — rasterise, hole-fill, NaN-off-patch, in-place rebuild — is exactly what the redesign should build on.

causes.title: PAD_SINK is one uniform 0.5mm constant for every contact geometry, and the tilt never re-contacts
causes.mechanism: A metal pad on a sidewall, a plastic saddle on the ridge, and a rim edge grazing the cheek all get the same 0.5mm interference allowance (nose.js:199-207). Combined with single-point tangency the frame reads as 'hovering, then uniformly pressed in 0.5mm'. Separately, the pantoscopic tilt pivots about the hang point (fit.js:418-434) but nothing re-checks contact after the pupil slide changed where the bridge column lands — the solve is one pass, hang->tilt->slide->push, with no iteration; the comment at fit.js:497-501 is explicit that this is by design (z cannot undo the earlier stages), which is sound for the current 1-DOF solve and becomes the thing to revisit once height and contact are coupled.
causes.evidence: nose.js:199-207 (PAD_SINK rationale and value); fit.js:495-522 (single-pass ordering, z-only by design)
causes.magnitude: Sub-millimetre per contact; cosmetic relative to causes 1-3, but it caps how good the contact can ever look even after they are fixed.
causes.fixDirection: Make sink a property of the contact sample (ridge vs sidewall from local field slope), or simply leave it until the equilibrium solve exists — it will mostly disappear into the two-sided bearing.

keep: The depth-field machinery in nose.js (buildFaceSurface, rasterise, fillHoles, depthAt, in-place rebuild — nose.js:65-196): rasterised front-surface at 1mm cells with NaN-off-patch semantics and zero-allocation rebuilds. A wedge-equilibrium redesign needs exactly this query layer; width-at-height and surface normals are derivable from the same Float32Array with no new data.

The model-side bridge sampling, findBridgeSurface (fit.js:202-236): asset-agnostic rearmost-per-bin back surface at 0.8mm cells, whole-column so unusual frames (brow-bar rests) stay expressible, with the cell size chosen by measurement (0.1mm overshoot). A two-pad solve consumes this same set split by side of centreline — the data is already right, only the reduction (max) is wrong. The hang-point finder findNoseContact and rake conditioning findFrontBox (fit.js:128-178, 249-293) are likewise sound.

The single-surface invariant and its enforcement: rebuildSurface's ordering guarantee that the seat field is rasterised from the very triangles that write the depth buffer (occluder.js:940-973), the derived relief OCCLUDER_RELIEF = PAD_SINK + feather + margin (occluder.js:132), and the harness block that pins field==mesh and no-frame-inside-head (pipeline-check.js:1193-1506). This is the hard-won architectural core — any redesign seats against surfaceOf(occluder) or it reintroduces the 50x27mm swallowing defect.

seat()'s bridge-relative formulation (nose.js:247-257 with fit.js:442-446): bridge anchor errors in x, y AND z cancel exactly out of the interference — the seat is immune to the borrowed-canonical-depth problem that afflicts absolute placement. Verified algebraically this session. A redesigned solve should keep all contact arithmetic in this relative frame.

The solvePlacement stage separation (fit.js:385-528) — scale, orientation, position, height, standoff as ordered, non-fighting corrections — and offsetZ applied after the seat so the standoff slider means vertex distance (fit.js:316-328). The stages will change meaning (height becomes an output), the discipline should survive.

SEAT_TAU easing living in frame.js (frame.js:64, 437-448) with reset-on-remeasure (frame.js:573-580): filtering the solved standoff, not the landmarks, at a named timescale, cleared on legitimate discontinuities. Right pattern, currently asked to hide too much noise.

pupilHeightInLens and widthVerdict (fit.js:539-574) as measurables — the optician-meaningful readouts a redesign should keep reporting, with pupil height repurposed from placement constraint to fit verdict.
opportunities: Nose width is measured every frame, medianed, deadbanded (anchors.js:398-449, frame.js:522-525, FIT_DEADBAND.noseWidth 0.2mm) and consumed by NOTHING in the seat since the warp removal (nose.js:230-245) — it is precisely the wedge parameter a resting-height equilibrium needs, already estimated and stabilised.

The field already contains the full wedge shape at 1mm resolution; width-at-height and sidewall normals are pure derived queries on the existing array (nose.js:65-131). The redesign's core physics needs no new measurement, only new reductions.

noseContacts carries the left/right pad populations (harness asserts spread across the centreline, pipeline-check.js:507-526) but max() erases sidedness — a two-bearing solve is a reduction change over existing data.

seat() already reports touched, interference, restedAt, clamped (nose.js:227, 263-268) and nothing asserts on them: no check that BOTH sides bear, no standoff-spread-across-faces check, no temporal stability check. The harness seats one frame at one static pose (yaw 22, pipeline-check.js:1216-1223) and asserts only non-penetration — 'good interaction' is currently unmeasured. Proposed measurables for the redesign: (1) two-sided bearing — worst gap of the SECOND-best side's contacts < ~0.8mm at rest; (2) resting-height law — across the six synthetic noses and across frames of different DBL, dHeight/dDBL in the physiological band (~1.5-2.5mm/mm from the canonical wedge), monotone; (3) standoff spread — vertex distance must VARY across the synthetic nose set (assert spread > ~1.5mm), not merely stay non-penetrating; (4) seat stability — with +-0.3mm synthetic landmark noise injected over a simulated second at 0/20/30-deg yaw and the diag roll+pitch pose, push RMS < 0.2mm and no single step > 0.5mm; (5) yaw-sweep contact integrity — pads stay clear of the drawn surface and within 1mm of the true skin across a +-30-deg sweep, not one angle.

diag/f00-f09 (ar/assets/samples/diag/) are the user's own complaint captures — roll+pitch on a pillow — consumed by nothing; measurables (2), (4), (5) can run against them directly, closing the loop on the exact poses complained about.

The measuring latch already freezes eyeLineY at difficult angles (frame.js:355-360), which means the seat's noise driver there is purely the field morph — so stabilising the seat does not require touching the anchor chain, only decoupling the resting solve's timescale from the occluder's per-frame shape easing.

jitter.mechanism: One frame's path to the rendered glasses matrix: camera frame → tracker (detect canvas long side 640, tracker.js:64; DEFAULT_NUM_FACES=2 at tracker.js:43 so MediaPipe's internal smoothing is OFF and landmarks arrive raw) → onDetection (main.js:819) → updatePose(detection, frame.captureDt) (main.js:865, 911) → updateFrame (frame.js:176). Inside updateFrame the final matrix is a product of two halves. (A) Head half: pose matrix decomposed (frame.js:185-190) → PoseSmoother.update then sample(lead=0) (frame.js:202-215; smoothing.js:614-643) — position through PredictedVector (One Euro law, minCutoff 0.6 / beta 1.2 / dCutoff 3.0, trendGain 0, smoothing.js:722), rotation through PredictedRotation (0.7 / 17.0, smoothing.js:725), scale through a fixed 0.6 Hz pole (smoothing.js:731); lag ceilings (3 cm / 20°) are backstops that never fire on jitter (smoothing.js:775-783) → composed into scene.head (frame.js:292). (B) Glasses-local half: anchors are re-measured EVERY frame under the RAW pose (frame.js:222-244; anchors.js:323-454), with each landmark's depth blended between borrowed-canonical and the per-frame depth fit by fitWeight = smoothstep(r2, 0.88, 0.92) (anchors.js:338-369; occluder.js:640-644), then clamped (anchors.js:485) — no temporal filter anywhere on this path. The per-frame anchor mix (frame.js:355-373): bridge and eyeCentreX are ALWAYS raw-observed; eyeLineY, bridgeUp, ears.y/z are raw-observed only inside the measuring latch (yaw<0.25≈9°, pitch<0.26, roll<0.30, exit at 1.15x, frame.js:26-49, 267-273) and median-carried outside it. solvePlacement (fit.js:385-528) then builds position = raw bridge target (fit.js:442-446) + pupil slide along bridgeUp scaled 1/max(up.y,0.2)≈1.22 with a 0.57 z-component (fit.js:464-493) + seat push; only the seat push is eased (SEAT_TAU 0.15 s, frame.js:64, 437-448); quaternion and scale are constants per fit settings. glasses.matrix composed at frame.js:450-452. The occluder mesh: shape offsets eased at SHAPE_TAU 0.10 s with per-vertex facing×visibility gains (occluder.js:171, 736-826), rebuilt through 0.2 mm / 2 mm drift deadbands (occluder.js:307-308), but TRANSLATED to the raw bridge every frame with no deadband (occluder.js:717-731). Temples aimed per frame from anchors.ears + placement.position (frame.js:463-471; temples.js:547-553). Screen conversion: pixelsPerCm = (viewHeight/2)/(z·tan(fov/2)) (frame.js:391-394) ≈ 17.4 px/cm ≈ 1.74 px/mm at 45 cm on a 960 px buffer. Net: screen jitter = (pose-filter residual, which self-opens under noise) + (raw landmark noise on bridge/eyeLine paths at transmission 1.0) + (episodic steps from gate flips, r2-band dither, and dropout-recovery snaps). The frame lock itself is airtight — none of the jitter is display-time shear.

causes.title: Rotation filter blown open at angle: the speed signal is rectified before smoothing, so noise reads as turn rate and beta=17 opens the cutoff
causes.mechanism: PredictedRotation feeds its adaptive cutoff `stepAxis.length()/dt` — the MAGNITUDE of the frame-to-frame rotation delta — into the 3 Hz rate low-pass (smoothing.js:466-471). A magnitude is always positive, so alternating-sign quaternion noise cannot cancel the way the position path's signed-then-abs treatment lets it (smoothing.js:217-225): pure noise produces a persistent DC 'turn rate'. cutoff = 0.7 + 17·rate (smoothing.js:473) then opens the filter exactly when measurement noise grows — which is precisely at 30-45° yaw, where half the landmarks feeding the Procrustes pose are hallucinated far-side points. There is no noise-adaptive term anywhere: the filter cannot distinguish 0.5 rad/s of jitter from 0.5 rad/s of turn.
causes.evidence: smoothing.js:466-473 (rectified rate), smoothing.js:725 (beta 17.0). Simulated with the exact shipped law at 30 fps, still head: at frontal noise (sigma 0.002 rad/frame) mean cutoff 1.85 Hz, transmission 0.42; at difficult-angle noise (sigma 0.015-0.025 rad/frame) the cutoff is driven to 9.3-15.1 Hz BY THE NOISE ALONE and transmission rises to 0.73-0.81 — the filter is nearly transparent. What-if with signed-rate smoothing (position's treatment): cutoff 3.3 Hz, transmission 0.64 at the same noise, with sweep-lag cost unchanged (0.0122 vs 0.0110 rad peak on a 20° 0.5 Hz sweep).
causes.magnitude: Output sigma 0.011-0.020 rad on the smoothed head; at the glasses' ~8 cm lever from the head origin that is 0.9-1.6 mm ≈ 1.5-2.8 px sigma, ~4-8 px peak-to-peak at 45 cm — the dominant continuous vibration at difficult angles. Frontal residual is 0.0008 rad ≈ 0.1 px (invisible), which is why the complaint is 'especially in difficult angles'.
causes.fixDirection: Smooth the SIGNED axis-angle step (per-axis omega components through the dCutoff pole, magnitude after) so noise cancels; then subtract a running noise floor (e.g. median absolute frame-to-frame delta over ~1 s) from the measured rate before beta multiplies it, for both rotation and position. Optionally scale beta down as a continuous function of pose difficulty (yaw/visibility), which the pipeline already computes.

causes.title: The bridge pin is completely unfiltered: raw landmark noise passes at transmission 1.0 into the glasses position AND the occlusion boundary, every frame, at every pose
causes.mechanism: The placement principle ('position re-measured from observed landmarks every frame') is implemented with zero conditioning: anchors.bridge = observed.bridge always (frame.js:357), placement target = bridge.x/y/z directly (fit.js:442-446), and the occluder is translated to the same raw bridge 'every frame and with no deadband' (occluder.js:717-731). With numFaces=2 (tracker.js:43) MediaPipe's upstream smoothing is off by design, so nothing between the detector and the screen touches this path. clampAnchors (anchors.js:485) bounds it but does not filter it. The pose filter can be perfect and the result still vibrates, because the glasses-local half of the matrix carries the raw noise; the occlusion boundary (far-lens cutoff) rides the same translation, so the most salient edge in the image jitters coherently with the frame. While the measuring latch is open (near-frontal), eyeLineY and bridgeUp are ALSO raw (frame.js:358-359), and eyeLineY noise is amplified 1.22x along bridgeUp with a 0.57 z-component (fit.js:489-492) — this is the frontal 'never stands completely still' shimmer.
causes.evidence: frame.js:355-373 (the raw/carried mix; bridge and eyeCentreX raw at every pose), fit.js:442-446, occluder.js:717-731, tracker.js:43 + smoothing.js:661-667 (numFaces contract), frame.js:494-506 (commitFit deadbands cover ONLY widths/metricScale — the 31-sample median stabilizes proportions, never the per-frame position inputs).
causes.magnitude: Frontal: bridge landmark noise ~0.1-0.2 mm face-space (estimated from unsmoothed FaceLandmarker at 640 px detect canvas) → 0.2-0.35 px sigma, plus the eyeLineY path adds a comparable term inside the latch → ~0.5 px combined, perceptible as fine shimmer against the frozen background. At 30-45° yaw: nose-region landmarks sit near the self-occlusion edge, noise 2-4x → 0.7-1.4 px sigma (3-6 px p-p) laterally, plus face-space z noise rotating into screen x as sin(yaw).
causes.fixDirection: Condition the pin without abandoning the principle: a sub-millimetre-scale One Euro or hysteresis deadband on the bridge in IMAGE space (zero lag on real motion, kills sub-noise motion), or a 3-frame median; drive its aggressiveness from the same measured-speed signal the pose filter already owns so a moving head is never lagged. Apply identically to the occluder translation so frame and boundary stay welded.

causes.title: The position filter has the same noise-as-speed failure: at angle its cutoff self-opens 4-6x and transmission nearly doubles
causes.mechanism: PredictedVector's cutoff = 0.6 + 1.2·speed where speed is the measured rate (smoothing.js:255, 326-345). The signed-rate smoothing at dCutoff 3.0 only partially cancels frame-to-frame noise (a 3 Hz pole passes ~20% of 15 Hz alternation, and the 3-axis quadrature sum of absolute values adds a positive bias), so larger measurement noise reads as speed and opens the filter — the classic One Euro high-noise failure, with no noise floor subtracted. Pose translation noise grows several-fold at 30-45° yaw (hallucinated far side degrades the Procrustes fit), so the filter is at its most open exactly when its input is at its worst.
causes.evidence: smoothing.js:96, 244-262, 331-345; constants smoothing.js:722. Simulated with the exact shipped law: sigma 0.02 cm/frame → cutoff 1.09 Hz, transmission 0.34 (matches the file's own '~1.1 Hz at rest' claim, validating the sim); sigma 0.08 cm → 2.6 Hz, 0.51; sigma 0.15 cm → 4.3 Hz, 0.61; sigma 0.25 cm → 6.8 Hz, 0.70.
causes.magnitude: At plausible yaw-pose translation noise (sigma 0.08-0.15 cm/frame) output sigma is 0.04-0.09 cm → 0.7-1.6 px sigma (3-6 px p-p) at 45 cm; frontal residual 0.007 cm ≈ 0.12 px. Comparable to the rotation term and additive with it.
causes.fixDirection: Same lever as rank 1: estimate the stationary noise floor from the running median absolute frame-to-frame delta and subtract it from measuredSpeed before beta; this preserves the measured 29.5 mm → 3.8 mm lag win because real head speeds (10-25 cm/s) sit far above the floor (~1-5 cm/s).

causes.title: Depth-fit dither: fitWeight is a memoryless function of per-frame r2 in a 0.04-wide band, stepping the bridge depth and pumping the occluder shape/seat chain
causes.mechanism: Every frame recomputes r2 of the landmark-z fit and maps it through smoothstep(0.88, 0.92) with peak slope 37.5 per unit r2 (occluder.js:640-644); the weight blends every recovered depth between borrowed-canonical and fitted (anchors.js:262, 364-369, bridge clamp ±1.6 cm at anchors.js:324). No temporal smoothing exists on r2, weight, or the coefficients (a is rebuilt from the RAW pose distance |e[14]| each frame, occluder.js:627-633). Inside the band, ordinary r2 jitter of ±0.005 moves the weight ~0.15-0.19, stepping the bridge z by that fraction of (solved−borrowed) — typically several mm at the nose. That z-step (a) enters the raw bridge target directly and rotates into screen x as sin(yaw); (b) shifts all 468 occluder depths, which the SHAPE_TAU ease turns into a 0.1 s breathing motion, trips the 0.2 mm surface-rebuild deadband (occluder.js:307, one frame's drift suffices), moves the seat field, and sends a new push target through the 0.15 s seat ease — the frame visibly breathes in and out. Prior review confirmed r2 INFLATES with yaw (rotation ramp dominates the variance), so the band-dither lives at the moderate 10-25° poses and the fit can report healthy on garbage at high yaw.

causes.title: The measuring latch swaps raw and carried anchors wholesale at ~9-10.4° of yaw: a discrete pop in height, standoff, and temple aim on every crossing
causes.mechanism: The latch (enter at yaw 0.25 ≈ 9° true per estimateYaw's calibration, exit at 1.15x; frame.js:267-273) gates a BINARY payload: eyeLineY, bridgeUp, and ears.y/z switch between raw-observed and median-carried values in one frame (frame.js:355-373). At the boundary the two differ by whatever drift the gate exists to protect against — 0.5-2 mm in eyeLineY — and that difference is amplified 1.22x along bridgeUp with a 0.57 z-component (fit.js:489-492), moves the seat solve's contact points across the curved nose field (fit.js:512-522), and steps both temple arms (temples.js:547-553). A wearer browsing in the 8-12° range — the commonest mirror pose — crosses the band repeatedly; the hysteresis stops per-frame chatter but every genuine crossing still lands the full step. estimateYaw is also roll-blind and saturates (tracker.js:383-394), so on the user's own pillow captures (roll+pitch) the gate's calibration is off in unmodeled ways.
causes.evidence: frame.js:26-49 (three gates), frame.js:267-273 (latch), frame.js:355-373 (binary payload), tracker.js:383-394, prior review: 0.25 ≈ 9° true yaw, saturates at 35.
causes.magnitude: 1-4 px vertical/standoff pop plus a temple-arm step, episodic at each band crossing rather than continuous — the 'twitch when I start to turn' component.
causes.fixDirection: Keep the latch for the sample window, but make the anchor payload a crossfade: blend observed↔carried over ~0.3 s or, better, weight continuously by the same pose-trust function (yaw/pitch/roll smoothsteps) so there is no boundary at all. Also stop using raw eyeLineY/bridgeUp even inside the latch — the median is already computed and is the better per-frame value (bridge stays the only live pin).

causes.title: Burst dropouts at 40-50° freeze-then-snap, and the recovery step is fed to the filter with a 2-4x understated dt
causes.mechanism: At 40-50° the landmarker fails in bursts; HOLD_FACELESS_RESULTS=4 rides them out by freezing frame+pose (main.js:722-738) — correct under the frame lock — but on the first face after a ~130 ms hold, updatePose passes dt = frame.captureDt (the ~33-66 ms submission interval, main.js:654-656, 865), not the true gap since the last APPLIED pose. The filter differences the new value against its pre-gap state over the short dt, overestimates speed up to 4x, the beta term blows the cutoff open, and the accumulated displacement lands in a single frame: a snap. Repeating every second or two at difficult angles, this alternates freeze/snap — a large part of 'figity' at exactly the poses under complaint.
causes.evidence: main.js:722-738 (hold), main.js:654-656 + 865 (captureDt is submission interval; faceless results do not advance the filter but do advance lastSubmitMs), smoothing.js:92, 222 (derivative over the passed dt), prior review: dropout-not-decay degradation, faceless bursts at 40-50°.
causes.magnitude: Head moving 10 cm/s during a 130 ms hold accumulates ~13 mm ≈ 20+ px arriving as one or two frame steps; even a slowly drifting head yields 3-6 px snaps.
causes.fixDirection: Track time-since-last-applied-detection and pass it as dt on recovery (the filters already handle variable dt correctly); optionally spread the correction over 2-3 frames via the existing soft lag-ceiling machinery, which is built for exactly this shape of correction.

keep: The frame-locked composite itself (main.js:642-701 snapshot-at-submission, main.js:844-850 pairing) — verified end to end during this review: no jitter component is display-time shear, which is the failure class this architecture eliminated. Any redesign keeps it untouched.

The PoseSmoother machinery (smoothing.js): Predicted/PredictedRotation structure, measured-rate speed signal, shared-speed vector treatment, the level→bound→trend ordering, lag ceilings as instrumented backstops with the `bounded` readout, split update/sample. The structure is sound and harness-pinned; only the speed-signal conditioning (sign handling + noise floor) needs work — that is a ~20-line change inside a keeper, not a rewrite.

The median + deadband fit estimate (FIT_WINDOW 31, FIT_DEADBAND, commitFit at frame.js:93-135, 507-538; medianAnchors at anchors.js:554-595) — proportions are provably jitter-free; none of the vibration traces to widths, metricScale, or the identity check. This is the model for how the per-frame anchor payload should also behave.

The seat-push easing pattern (SEAT_TAU with the eased-minus-raw compensation at frame.js:437-448) — the correct template for filtering a face-space constant without lagging position; a redesign should extend this pattern to the other face-space constants (eyeLineY, bridgeUp), not remove it.
The single-surface guarantee (occluder.js: surfaceOf, rebuildSurface ordering) — seat and drawn occluder are the same triangles by construction; this is the invariant and it held under inspection.

The facing ramp + self-occlusion visibility grid (occluder.js:195-247, 843-929) — the right mechanism for far-side hallucination, and the per-vertex trust weights it produces are exactly the confidence signal the rest of the pipeline should be consuming (see opportunities).
The hysteresis-latch pattern for pose gates (frame.js:267-273) — right idea for stopping per-frame chatter; only its binary payload needs to become a crossfade.
The instrumentation culture: window.__ar, depthClamped, rebuild counters, `bounded` percentage, the restedAt report in seat() — a redesign should extend this (add a jitter readout), not rebuild it.
The detect-rotation search and re-aim for rolled faces (main.js:749-817) — the only roll handling in the pipeline and it works; the pillow captures depend on it.
opportunities: A noise-floor estimate is one line away and nothing computes it: PredictedVector already has measuredSpeed and the per-frame residual (value − level); a running median absolute delta over ~1 s is the stationary noise sigma, and subtracting it from the speed signal is the published fix for One Euro's high-noise failure. Same signal fixes both position and rotation filters and could gate the bridge pin.

state.sampleSet holds 31 complete anchor sets (frame.js:283-287) — the frame-to-frame variance of observed.bridge, eyeLineY, and ears is sitting in memory every frame and nothing reads it: a free, live, per-field jitter meter that could drive adaptive deadbands and a readout.

Continuous yaw from the pose quaternion is already half-used: frame.js:249-251 takes pitch and roll from the pose euler but the gate and readouts use estimateYaw (saturating at ~35°, roll-blind, tracker.js:383-394). The same YXZ euler yields a continuous, non-saturating yaw for trust ramps at no cost.

The visibility grid's per-vertex `behind` and the facing weights (occluder.js:797-810) quantify per-landmark observability every frame, but only the occluder consumes them — the bridge pin, the pose filter's trust, and the measuring gate could all be weighted by the observability of the landmarks they stand on.
data.depthFit persists across frames but is overwritten memorylessly (occluder.js:747); it is the natural home for an EMA over r2/weight/b that would kill the band dither with three lines.

diag/f00-f09 (ar/assets/samples/diag/) are the user's own complaint captures — roll+pitch on a pillow — and are consumed by nothing. Replaying them through updateFrame and measuring the screen-px std and max-step of the composed glasses matrix is the jitter regression harness this diagnosis has no ground truth for; every magnitude above marked 'estimated' becomes a measurement there.

The harness pins lag (the 29.5→3.8 mm story in smoothing.js) but has no stillness-at-yaw test: 'does not shimmer' exists only for the frontal case; a still-head-at-35° synthetic with realistic landmark noise would have caught ranks 1-3 before a user did.
captureDt vs time-since-applied-detection: both timestamps already exist in state (lastSubmitMs, lastResultMs, main.js:699, 873); the correct recovery dt is a subtraction away.

causes.title: The single bridge pin is pose-dependent: the whole seat rides an anchor that wanders millimetres across the user's own poses
causes.mechanism: Everything hangs from anchors.bridge, re-derived each frame from one landmark carried to a depth-fit-corrected borrowed depth. On a rigid face this point should be a face-space constant; measured across the user's ten pillow captures it moves 6.8 mm in x (tracking yaw at ~0.2 mm/deg: +3.2 mm at -17.7 deg yaw, -3.6 mm at +10.4 deg) and 5.0 mm in z (55.8 mm at pitch -16 deg vs 61.0 mm frontal). The occluder translation (occluder.js:719-725), the frame pin (fit.js:442-451), and the seat's shiftZ (nose.js:247) all follow it, so the frame and the nose surface both slide and push with pose while the drawn face does not.
causes.evidence: frame.js:355-357 (bridge live at every pose, by design); occluder.js:719-725; nose.js:247; probe: bridge anchor mean per still f00-f09 = x [-3.58..+3.23] mm, z [55.82..60.99] mm on one person
causes.fixDirection: Exploit rigidity: fuse the bridge (and depth offset) temporally in face space — a robust running estimate updated by observation, not re-derived from scratch — so per-pose systematic error and per-frame noise both cancel without adding pose lag
causes.magnitude: 2-5 mm of lateral/standoff placement error across +/-10-18 deg yaw and -16 deg pitch (the complaint regime)

causes.title: The standoff is not a face constant: seat push swings 2.4 mm with pose and flips regime with the measuring gate
causes.mechanism: Raw seat push on the same face measures -6.0..-6.2 mm at near-frontal measured-anchor frames and -3.5..-4.4 mm at yawed/pitched gate-closed frames (interference -5.5 mm vs -3.1 mm before push). Two couplings: the deformed surface is deliberately view-dependent (ray-pinning at the current pose), and when the gate closes the anchors revert/freeze to canonical (noseWidthRatio 1.000 vs measured 0.952-0.962). SEAT_TAU (0.15 s) then drags each transition as a visible ~0.3 s in/out re-seat while the head turns — the frame breathes against the nose exactly during pose changes.
causes.evidence: frame.js:26/38/49 (gates), frame.js:437-448 + frame.js:52-64 (SEAT_TAU); nose.js:226-278; probe: seat rawPush mean per still, bimodal on gates.measuringFraction (f01/f03/f08 = -6.01/-6.02/-6.19 mm measuring=1; f00/f02/f04/f05/f06/f09 = -4.09/-4.00/-3.57/-4.18/-3.64/-4.40 mm measuring=0)
causes.fixDirection: Make the standoff a converged face-space constant (fused like the fit, not re-solved per pose); solve residual contact per-frame only as a bounded correction
causes.magnitude: ~2.4 mm standoff swing between poses of one face; per-frame noise is only 0.05-0.15 mm sd — the instability is systematic, not noise

causes.title: The 'nose' the frame seats on is the average nose bent by ~6 sparse, noisy landmarks — and in the complaint regime it is not personalised at all
causes.mechanism: The seat field is the canonical mesh deformed by ray-pinned landmarks; only ~6 landmarks describe the nose (tip 4, bridge 6, sidewalls 245/465/114/343), spaced 3-7 mm, so the sidewall shape between them — where pads actually bear, falling 8 mm per cm — is subdivision interpolation of the average nose. Nose width, the input that moves pad-line skin 2 mm per 15%, is only measured while the gate is open; on 5 of the user's 10 captures it never opens, so a session lived on the pillow seats against a canonical-width nose forever.
causes.evidence: canonical-face.js:16-38 (LM table); nose.js:47-48 (sidewall gradient), nose.js:56-58 (vertex spacing); occluder.js:736-826; probe: noseWidthRatio pinned at 1.000 (sd 0) on all gate-closed stills vs 0.952-0.962 measured
causes.fixDirection: A dedicated nose capture: aggregate the dense nose-region landmarks (not just 6) across frames and poses into a converged personal nose patch, refined silently in the background (no scan phase), with the depth dimension anchored by multi-pose parallax rather than single-frame z
causes.magnitude: 1-2 mm contact-surface error from shape interpolation; up to 2 mm more from unmeasured nose width in the gate-closed regime

causes.title: Seat solves along camera +Z at every pose, so 'standoff' changes meaning as the head turns
causes.mechanism: seat() pushes along the view axis (deliberate, so it cannot fight the height solve). At 18 deg yaw the view axis is 5% foreshortened against the face normal and the same push slides contacts laterally across a sidewall falling 8 mm/cm — a continuous pose-dependence layered on top of the gate bimodality (f07, gate open at 4.3 deg yaw, already sits at -4.7 mm between the -6.0 frontal and -3.6 yawed regimes).
causes.evidence: nose.js:210-225 (comment and code), fit.js:495-522; probe: push vs yaw is continuous, not purely gate-driven
causes.fixDirection: Solve the standoff along the face-space nose normal on the fused surface; convert to camera axis at composite time
causes.magnitude: sub-millimetre directly (cos 18 deg = 0.95), but it couples the push to yaw continuously — part of the measured 2.4 mm swing

causes.title: The depth-trust gate is uninformative exactly where it matters: r2 RISES with pose severity and the 0.88-0.92 blend never engages
causes.mechanism: fitLandmarkDepth's r2 correlates MediaPipe z with canonical camera depth across all 468 points, so the global rotation ramp dominates it: measured r2 is 0.965-0.972 on frontal faces and 0.982-0.9955 on every hard capture — highest of all twelve stills (0.9955) at pitch -16 deg, where borrowed depths and hallucinated far-side landmarks are worst. Weight saturates at 1.0 on all 12 stills (sd 0), depthClamped = 0 — the carefully built blend is a constant, and MediaPipe z is fully trusted at every pose. The prior finding (single calibration point at 10.6 deg yaw; inflation with yaw) is confirmed on the user's own captures.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:596-644 (r2, weight), occluder.js:289-304 (thresholds); probe: r2 mean per still (face-a 0.972, face-b 0.965, f06 0.9955, f04 0.986, f07 0.994), weight mean/sd = 1/0 everywhere
causes.fixDirection: Replace global r2 with a nose-region residual against the current fused shape (region-restricted, rotation-ramp removed), and validate depth across poses (parallax consistency), not within one frame
causes.magnitude: gate is inert: 0 modulation observed across 720 production-path frames; depth error passes at full weight precisely at hard poses

causes.title: The nose tip is the noisiest landmark on the face, and the nose has the fewest constraints
causes.mechanism: Under identical injected sensor noise the nose tip moves 1.5-2x more than the sidewall landmarks and 2-3x more than eye corners; at pitch -16 deg (f06, blurred) its y-noise is 2.16 px sd vs 0.34 px frontal — a 6.4x amplification. The scan of the nose is therefore built from the least reliable observations on the face, with no temporal aggregation (SHAPE_TAU easing is a low-pass on a per-frame full re-measurement, not an estimator).
causes.evidence: probe landmark table: noseTip sd (x,y) px — face-b (0.57,0.34), f04 (1.18,0.87), f06 (1.43,2.16); sidewalls 0.3-0.9 px
causes.fixDirection: Weight the nose capture by measured per-landmark stability; aggregate over time and poses instead of trusting each frame's tip
causes.magnitude: 0.3-0.6 px landmark noise frontal, 0.9-2.2 px at the user's poses (x2-6); at 42 px/cm that is 0.2-0.5 mm per frame on the defining landmark

The 'scan of the face isn't good enough' is partly that in his regime there is no scan.
causes.evidence: frame.js:26/38/49, frame.js:267-273 (latch); tracker.js:383-394; probe: measuringFraction = 0 on f00/f02/f04/f05/f06/f09, noseWidthRatio 1.000 there; face-a itself sits at imgYaw 0.2494 — a hair under the gate

causes.magnitude: 50% of complaint captures unpersonalised; gate threshold ~9 deg true yaw vs the 25% (~14 deg) it claims

causes.title: The bridge pin is deliberately unfiltered, so landmark noise bypasses the (excellent) pose smoother and reaches the screen
causes.mechanism: The composite = smoothed head pose x raw per-frame bridge anchor. PoseSmoother output noise measured at <=0.1 deg / 0.04 mm — the pose stack is not the leak. But anchors.bridge is re-measured raw every frame with no deadband and no filter (documented as the placement principle), so its 0.05-0.20 mm/frame noise (x42 px/cm) lands directly in the drawn frame: measured screen jitter of the placed frame origin 0.12-0.30 px sd frontal, 0.38-0.56 px at hard poses — under injected noise 2-4x weaker than a real dim-room webcam, and without motion blur. Scaled to reality this is the 1-2.5 px 'vibrates a little, doesn't stand still'.
causes.evidence: occluder.js:713-718 ('position from the landmarks, every frame and with no deadband'); frame.js:355-357, 432-436; probe: screenXpx/screenYpx sd per still; smoothed pose position sd 0.0-0.2 mm, angles 0.05-0.32 deg

causes.title: Detector noise response amplifies x2-6 at the user's 'difficult angles', and motion blur multiplies it again
causes.mechanism: The detector is bit-for-bit deterministic on frozen pixels (all sds = 0.000 over 60 repeats), so all jitter is response to input pixel change. The response is strongly pose-dependent: same injected noise produced 2-3x the pose-angle noise (0.05-0.15 deg frontal to 0.14-0.32 deg hard) and up to 6.4x the nose-tip noise at pitch -16 deg; the two visibly blurred captures (f06, f07) are the worst two. 'Especially difficult angles' is the detector's own sensitivity curve.
causes.evidence: probe run 1 (no noise): every sd 0.000 on 12 stills; run 2 (sigma 2.2DN): pose/landmark/screen sd tables; f07 eyeInnerL x-sd 2.10 px
causes.fixDirection: Accept as a property of MediaPipe; design the pipeline to spend this noise where it is invisible (temporal fusion of face-space constants) and scale filter bandwidth with a live sensor-noise estimate (frame differencing)
causes.magnitude: amplification factor frontal-to-hard: x2-3 pose angles, x2-6 nose landmarks, x2-4.5 on-screen

causes.title: Regime-switch machinery sits exactly astride the user's poses: gate flips step the anchors and re-seat the frame

The user's pillow poses (yaw -18..+10 deg) cross this boundary constantly, so the frame periodically re-settles — read as 'doesn't stand still'. The 1.15x latch hysteresis covers estimator chatter but not real motion through the band.
causes.evidence: frame.js:267-273 (latch), 344-373 (live/carried split), 437-448 (seat easing); probe: seat bimodality and measuringFraction split across f00-f09

causes.magnitude: ~2.2 mm seat step + ear/eye-line steps per flip, each a visible ~0.3 s settle

causes.title: The seat surface is rebuilt nearly every frame — the 0.2 mm rebuild deadband does not hold under sensor noise

causes.fixDirection: Deadband on the surface's effect (seat push / boundary position), not on accumulated vertex drift; or rebuild on the fused shape's schedule once the shape is an estimator rather than a per-frame measurement
